summary.headline: Himadri Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose to INR 1,543 crore (+44% YoY) and PAT to INR 240 crore (+28%), while per-tonne EBITDA eased sequentially to about INR 21,000.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 standalone EBITDA was INR 308 crore (+27% YoY) and PAT INR 240 crore (+28% YoY); consolidated revenue was INR 1,691 crore and PAT INR 231 crore (+31%). Management attributed the sequential per-tonne EBITDA dip (from about INR 22,700-22,800 to about INR 21,000) to a raw-material pass-through lag, higher freight costs, and a higher export share (33% vs 26%). New carbon nanotube, LFP and anthraquinone/carbazole capacities are on schedule, with commissioning timelines reiterated, and the proposed merger of the Birla Tyres business into Himadri was announced. Mining is expected to restart this quarter after environmental clearance was received.

segments.name: Carbon black (speciality / core)
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation was 88% in Q2 FY27, with guidance of 88-95%; volume grew about 14,000 tonnes QoQ per management, after the 70,000 TPA commissioning. All new materials (CNT, super speciality carbon black) will be reported within the carbon segment.

segments.name: Birla Tyres (under Dalmia Bharat Refractories, trading for Himadri)
segments.commentary: Q2 trading revenue was about INR 140 crore at about INR 1 crore EBITDA (trading margin). Management says it is on track for breakeven and reiterated its top-line guidance; numbers will be added to Himadri on consolidation after the proposed merger.

segments.name: Mining (sand, West Bengal)
segments.commentary: No revenue in the quarter; it carried negative EBITDA because environmental clearance was pending. Clearance was received in October 2026, with operations to start in Q3 FY27 and a longer-term revenue potential of about INR 500 crore.

guidance_outlook: Maintains target of INR 1,100 crore+ PAT by FY28, to be supported by core business and new capacity commissioning.
Per-tonne EBITDA is guided to a range of about INR 20,000-24,000 going forward; management says it is confident of staying above INR 20,000 on a sustainable basis.

Capex spend of about INR 250 crore in Q2 FY27; total FY27 spend guided at INR 800-900 crore. Management said the roughly INR 1,500 crore programme over two years will be funded from internal accruals, not debt.
Most new capacity is expected to show full impact from FY29, per the analyst's read of management's reply.
Management expects working capital to normalise over the next two quarters and operating cash flow to turn positive on an annual basis.
Anthraquinone/carbazole (5,300 TPA) is now targeted for full commissioning together in Q4 FY27 instead of two phases, with about 9 months of full operation next year.
capex_capacity: Carbon nanotube (CNT): 200 TPA facility targeted for commissioning in Q4 FY27; production start stated as Q4 FY27.
LFP cathode active material: initial 2,000 TPA trial production in Q3 FY27, with samples to OEMs in Q4 FY27; next phase of 40,000 TPA deferred to end-FY28 so that qualifications are in place first.
Super speciality carbon black: planned 6,000 TPA targeted for Q4 FY28.
Anthraquinone and carbazole: 5,300 TPA total, with both phases commissioned together by Q4 FY27 to avoid a three-month shutdown.

Silicon carbon anode: engineering under way; formal capex and timeline to be announced later. Synthetic graphite anode plant has commenced operation, and samples have been shared with domestic and global customers.
demand_pricing: Volume grew 11% YoY in Q2 FY27 (1,46,000 tonnes cited on the call); revenue rose 58% YoY, driven by volume and higher raw-material-linked selling prices.
Export share rose to 33% of sales from 26% a year earlier; higher container freight rates, linked to the geopolitical situation, weighed on margins.
Gross margin fell about 500 bps YoY on a standalone basis, which management attributed to a raw-material pass-through lag, with 9-10 days of raw-material inventory held.
Management says realisations move with raw-material prices and should not be extrapolated; sequential per-tonne EBITDA is expected to vary between quarters.
Battery materials: management expects pricing to be in line with Chinese suppliers; anode products are at sample stage, with no realisation guidance given.
Carbon black demand described as robust; ENERGEX grades received approval for high-voltage cable and battery applications and have started commercial orders.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the sharp gross margin moderation, and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are stable and that per-tonne EBITDA was about INR 21,000 vs INR 17,900 YoY and INR 22,700-22,800 QoQ. The dip was attributed to pricing pass-through timing, higher freight and a higher export share, all described as temporary.

qa_highlights.question: Are the new LFP, anthraquinone and carbazole products margin-accretive from start?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed yes, saying they would add to incremental margin from the start. For LFP, margin guidance was deferred until commercial discussions begin after the 2,000 TPA plant.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex has been spent, and what is planned for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 250 crore spent in Q2 FY27, with INR 800-900 crore expected in FY27. Commercial dates for projects fall before FY28, so most capacity impact is expected from FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and revenue potential of mining?
qa_highlights.answer: Environmental clearance was received in October 2026 and operations are to start in the current quarter. The longer-term top-line potential is about INR 500 crore, depending on volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why did carbon black EBITDA per tonne fall vs the peer, and is there a sweet spot from coal tar?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said raw-material prices are correlated, so there is no pricing edge. The advantage is clean, self-produced feedstock for speciality carbon black, and the decline was attributed to freight and export mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the funding plan for the remaining capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the programme of about INR 1,500 crore over two years will be funded entirely through internal accruals. Working-capital debt was used earlier, and it is expected to come down over the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the commissioning and approval timeline for the LFP and anode products?
qa_highlights.answer: The LFP 2,000 TPA plant is to start trial production in Q3 FY27, with samples in Q4 and customer qualification taking 12-18 months. The 40,000 TPA expansion was deferred to end-FY28 so that approvals are in place first.

risks_watch: Gross and per-tonne EBITDA variability from raw-material pass-through lags, freight costs and export mix; management says per-tonne EBITDA could range INR 20,000-24,000.
Commissioning of CNT (Q4 FY27), LFP 2,000 TPA (Q3 FY27) and anthraquinone/carbazole 5,300 TPA (Q4 FY27), with the anthraquinone/carbazole phases now combined.
Long customer qualification cycles for battery materials (management cited about 12-18 months), so commercial volumes remain uncertain.
Proposed Birla Tyres merger is subject to statutory, regulatory, creditor and shareholder approvals.
Working capital at 37% of sales vs 31.3% a year ago; receivable days rose to 65 from 63 QoQ.
Mining restart in Q3 FY27 following clearance; revenue contribution not yet visible.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the growth pipeline and the business model's resilience, but defensive on the sequential margin decline, which was attributed to temporary factors. Management avoided giving specific margin, realisation or LFP economics, deferring these to later updates.
key_quotes: So per metric ton EBITDA is around 21,000, which in the sequential quarter was at around 22,700-22,800 and in the corresponding quarter, that is last year, it was at around 17,900.
We are confident of achieving EBITDA above 20,000 on a sustainable basis, and this will strengthen in the quarters to come.
We remain confident in achieving our previously guided target of INR 1,100 crores plus PAT by FY28.
So everything will be through internal accrual.
